title: Causal Analysis of Over-Refusal: The False Positive Chain

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain with important counterfactual: over-refusal drives users to less safe alternatives, potentially causing net harm. Reframes what passing a safety benchmark actually means.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running refusal rate measurements is doable, but the counterfactual displacement modeling requires economic or behavioral modeling skills that go beyond standard ML fundamentals.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Quantifying the over-refusal/under-refusal tradeoff curve is focused, but adding the counterfactual net-harm modeling extends the scope into sustained analytical effort.

novelty.reasoning: Over-refusal as a failure mode is actively studied. ORFuzz (2508.11222, confirmed at ASE 2025) directly studies over-refusal fuzzing. Research on refusal mechanisms using sparse autoencoders exists (ACL 2025 findings). The specific counterfactual displacement modeling -- quantifying net harm from users switching to unfiltered models due to over-refusal -- is a novel framing not found in existing literature. The tradeoff curve idea is partially novel but the problem space is well-explored.
